title: Joint Subspace Sparse Attention: 6.4x Long-Context Decoding

beats.text: Before you train your next model, see how Joint Subspace Sparse Attention cuts 6.43x of memory overhead.
beats.visual_focus: A glowing neural network flickering as it chokes on massive data streams.

beats.text: The KV-cache is the villain. It forces your GPU to fetch useless tokens, like a librarian retrieving every book in the building for one sentence.
beats.visual_focus: A massive, cluttered bookshelf collapsing under the weight of redundant data blocks.

beats.text: JSSA shatters this by learning a shared low-dimensional subspace, isolating only the critical tokens needed for accurate attention.
beats.visual_focus: A complex cloud of vectors collapsing into a clean, sharp, low-dimensional manifold.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—hitting the 'memory bandwidth' pain point immediately is exactly what I want to hear. I didn't cringe at any 'smart drawer' metaphors, which is a huge plus. I got lost for a second on the 'gather-free kernel' part; I know what a kernel is, but I'm not 100% sure why the 'gather' operation is the specific bottleneck being bypassed here without a quick visual or one-sentence clarification.
